title: Duke of Sessa to Charles V, Rome, 18 April 1524, RAH Salazar A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877-R9878)

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877, R9878 duplicate)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter or its duplicate; Bergenroth's CSP Spain vol. 2 skips it. Sibling letters in the same cipher carry the court's decipherments (ff. 140, 172, 324).

transcription.source: DECODE images (R9877, R9878), cut into token tiles by tokens.py
transcription.notes: Nine cipher lines (eight on f. 128r, one on f. 128v); the duplicate ff. 130-131 is token-for-token the same. The transcription file mixes two passes and clear text, so it cannot be measured as it stands.

system.summary: Mixed nomenclator: three-letter code groups for words, names and syllables plus single letters and signs for spelling, with a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
system.sibling_key: Same cipher as Sessa's decrypted despatches of 1523-25 (ff. 138/140, 168-172, 322-324; R9897, R9893, R9834 and others); the key was rebuilt from them.
system.notes: About 110 code groups and the letter alphabet recovered (README). Homophones: several code variants (no ler/lex, con tat/tar). f~ switches clear/cipher; 'v db' is a null opener.

prior_solution.where: DECODE lists it Non-decrypted; not in CSP Spain; only sibling letters carry decipherments

conditions.human_role: Downloaded DECODE images logged in and supplied the DECODE cookie

solution.what: Identified DECODE's '1424' as 1524, the Duke of Sessa, Salazar A-31, and located the decrypted siblings in CSP Spain vol. 2.
Cut every cipher line of f. 128 and the siblings into token tiles; collated the duplicate f. 130.
Passes 1-9: aligned sibling ciphers (ff. 138, 168v, 170-171, 322) against their clears to assign code and letter values.
Passes 10-13: 1525 and July 1524 siblings (R9897, R9898, R9893) settled rad, lif, hud, zum and others.
Pass 14: template matching over the seven 1523 decrypted letters gave z y = -on; vo, per, ruc, hay remain unattested.
Word-level reading of the nine cipher lines, with four groups and one clause open.

Retry of the open groups (vo, per, ruc, hay, m-re clause) with the pass-15 key over the new full R9660 transcription; ruc gets five contexts (a verb/adjective root), none fixes a value; vo/per absent.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The code values were rebuilt by aligning deciphered sibling letters in the same RAH Salazar A-31 volume (ff. 138/140, 170-172, 322-324, R9893 f. 483/485) and other Sessa letters of 1523-25 with their contemporary clears; the rebuilt key was then applied to ff. 128-131.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription_f128.txt pass-2 lines P1-P8: 116 cipher tokens (nulls counted, f~ switches and clear excluded); unread: vo, per, rus, hay (4) and the unresolved clause 'los m-re que r-ido los que no m-r-e-van' plus the end 'r-[...]' (~10); 102/116
outcome.notes: Residue: vo, per, ruc, hay, and the clause 'los m-re que r-ido'. fraction_read measured on transcription_f128.txt (102 of 116 tokens read). Key partial: 4 code groups unattested and one letter-sign value (probably v) wrong.
